texts.preamble: Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma vs Sh. Som Pal Singh on 4 December, 2019 In The Court Of Sh. Yashwant Kumar District & Sessions Judge/Fsat, New Delhi In the matter of : Fsat No. 10/19 (Cnr No. Dlnd010059202019) Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma S/o Sh. Som Dutt Sharma M/s Om Dairy 6132, BlockI, Dev Nagar, Karol Bagh New Delhi110 005. R/o 6156, Block No. 1, Gali No. 5 Dev Nagar, Karol Bagh, New Delhi110005. ..... Appellant Versus 1. Sh. Som Pal Singh Food Safety Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Place New Delhi110001. 2. Designated Officer Department of Food Safety Govt. of Nct of Delhi 8th Floor, Mayur Bhawan, Connaught Place New Delhi110001. ..... Respondents Appeal Against The Order Dated 28.02.2019 Of Ld. Adjudicating Officer / Additional District Magistrate (Central), New Delhi. Fsat No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. Fso & Anr. Page No. 1 of 7 Date of filing of appeal : 27.03.2019 Date of arguments : 02.12.2019 Date of judgment : 04.12.2019 J U D G M E N T :
texts.facts: Briefly stating, the facts as per the appeal are that on 16.04.2018, a sample of "Mixed Milk" was lifted by the Food Safety Officer (in short FSO) from the premises of appellant i.e. M/s Om Diary, Shop No. 6132, BlockI, Dev Nagar, Karol Bagh, New Delhi110005. On analysis by the Food Analyst, Delhi, the said sample was declared to be substandard vide report dt.24.04.2018 due to the presence of milk powder which should not be present as per the definition of mixed milk laid down under Regulation 1.2.11 of the Food Safety & Standards (Food Products FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 2 of 7 Standards & Food Additives) Regulation, 2011. After receipt the said report of Food Analyst, Delhi, the appellant herein was provided with an opportunity to file an appeal under Section 46(4) of the FSS Act within the stipulated period of 30 days. Consequently, a complaint was filed against the appellantherein by the FSO before the Adjudicating Officer. After pleadings and enquiry, the Ld. ADM passed the impugned order dated 28.02.2019 imposing a penalty of Rs.1,50,000/ upon the appellant. 3. The appellant has challenged the impugned order inter alia on the grounds among others that the Ld. ADM has failed to appreciate that the Food Analyst has not given the percentage of milk powder. The sample was also fit for human consumption. The test skimmed milk powder was found to be positive. Ld. Adjudication Officer did not conduct fair enquiry in a legal way or that no departmental witness or other witnesses were examined. 4. The Ld. Chief PP for the State has not filed reply to the appeal, however, he has opposed the appeal. Even, the sampled commodity was fit for human consumption FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 3 of 7 and the same was not injurious to health. The FSO while lifting the sample followed the faulty procedure. The Ld. ADM did not examine the witnesses for the proper adjudication of this matter. Therefore, the impugned order has been rightly FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr.
texts.arguments: Counsel for the appellant argued that the Food Analyst has not given percentage of milk powder in the sample taken from the FBO. Ld. Counsel for the appellant, in support of his arguments, has relied upon the judgments in the cases of State (Delhi Admn.) versus Madan Gupta and another 2007(1) FAC 186; M/s Indana Spices and Food Industries Ltd. versus Food Inspector, Bhiwani in Criminal Misc. No. 1412M of 1991 decided by Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court on 16.12.1991; Sain Dass versus The State of Haryana 2010 (1) FAC Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma vs Sh. Som Pal Singh on 4 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/141237757/ 2 17; State of Haryana versus Sat Narain 2003 (2) FAC 378; Khyber Agro Farms Pvt. Ltd. versus The State of Jammu and Kashmir & Ors. 2018 (2) FAC 254; Nemi Chand versus State of Rajasthan 2016 (1) FAC 561 and State of Govt of NCT of Delhi versus Jagdish Tyagi 2017(2) FAC 521. 7. The Ld. Chief Public Prosecutor argued that as the powder is prohibited in the milk, there is no question of showing percentage of powder in the report. The milk powder was found in the sample and it was not natural milk and the same has also been considered by the Ld. ADM in the impugned order dt.28.02.2019. In the natural milk, no powder can be mixed. The standards and parameters, which have been laid down by the legislature are to be followed but the appellant has not followed it for selling the milk in this case. The substandard milk is to be treated as an adulterated article, even if it has not caused injuries to health. The appellant did not comply with the standards of rules / regulations of Food Safety and Standard Act. . The Ld. Chief PP for the State, in support of his arguments relied upon the judgment in the case of Raj Kumar versus The State of Uttar Pradesh in Criminal Appeal No. 1541 of 2019 decided on 04.10.2019 by the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India 8. 11. Section 26 of the FSS Act 2006 provides responsibilities of the Food Business Operator. Sub clause (2)(ii) of Section 26 the said Act provides that no Food Business Operator shall himself or by any person on FSAT No. 10/19 Sh. Guru Dutt Sharma. vs. FSO & Anr. Page No. 5 of 7 his behalf manufacturer, store, sell or distribute any article of food which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter. Section 26 of the FSS Act, 2006, seeks to provide for the responsibilities of the food business operator to ensure that the articles of food satisfy the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations made thereunder at all stages of production, processing, import, distribution and sale within the businesses under his control. Subclause (2) provides that no food business operator shall himself or by any person on his behalf manufacturer, store, sell or distribute any article of food which is misbranded or substandard or contains extraneous matter or which is for the time being prohibited by the Food Authority or the Central Government or the State Government in the interest of public health.
